title: China Completes First Construction Stage at Antelope Reef, Satellite Images Show — Largest South China Sea Base Yet
detail: Satellite imagery reviewed by Reuters and published August 19, 2026 shows China has completed the first stage of construction at Antelope Reef (Lingyang Jiao) in the Paracel Islands, reclaiming an island roughly 6km (4 miles) long with a straight coastline exceeding 3km — long enough, analysts say, to support a future runway. A 680-meter wharf now fronts a deep-water harbor, with a China Coast Guard vessel photographed alongside, and a helicopter pad has been built in the southeast corner. Barges and dredgers have left the site after more than six months of work. PLATracker analyst Ben Lewis said 'the northern part of the South China Sea would be particularly important in a Taiwan conflict scenario, so Antelope is ideally placed,' and noted the base could eventually host H-6 strategic bombers. China's defense ministry did not respond to Reuters' request for comment; state media have described the facility's purpose as weather forecasting and scientific research, which analysts dispute given the wharf, helipad and runway-length coastline. China has occupied the Paracels since seizing them from South Vietnam in 1974.

media.caption: Satellite imagery shows the reclaimed island at Antelope Reef, Paracel Islands, after China completed the first construction stage

title: Malaysia's Anwar Cites US-Backed Philippine Balabac Base in Pledge to Reinforce Sabah Defenses
detail: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on August 19, 2026 that the Philippines' expansion of military infrastructure on Balabac Island, southern Palawan — including a new 3-kilometer airstrip and naval facilities funded in part through the US Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA) — has raised concern in Kuala Lumpur, given the island's proximity (roughly 50km, about 20 minutes by vessel) to Malaysia's Banggi Island in Sabah. Anwar said 'as a neighbouring country closely affected by claims over Sabah, we are somewhat concerned with the tension,' while stressing that bilateral relations with Manila 'remain very good' and that Malaysia lacks the resources to match Balabac's scale. He announced plans to reinforce Sabah's defenses with additional battalions, a new 155mm artillery regiment, coastal radar systems, a Turkish-built Multi-Purpose Command Platform, and ANKA reconnaissance drones. Balabac is one of nine EDCA sites in the Philippines and sits roughly 330km from the center of the Spratly Islands, flanking the Sulu Sea passage.
